title: When overwriting keyboard shortcuts from system tray settings it's possible to close the main window before answering the modal that asks for confirmation
line: The shortcut conflict question now blocks the settings window it came from, so it can't be closed underneath and Continue assigns the shortcut.
explanation: KeySequenceHelper::showQuestionDialog() and showErrorDialog() create a KMessageDialog with no parent and set Qt::WindowModal. A window-modal dialog only blocks its transient parent, and this one had none, so the System Tray Settings window stayed fully usable: it could be closed under the 'Found Conflict' question, which then stayed on screen alone and whose Continue acted on a destroyed recorder. The change makes both dialogs transient for the window the KeySequenceItem lives in before showing them, so the settings window is blocked until the question is answered. This is the same patch as Niccolò's open MR frameworks/kdeclarative!286.

commits.message:
KeySequenceItem: make the conflict dialog block its window

The settings window could be closed under the shortcut conflict dialog.
The dialog had no parent window, so its window modality blocked nothing.
Make it and the error dialog transient for the shortcut's window.

BUG: 519304

media.caption: Master: 'Found Conflict' after pressing Ctrl+F1 on Audio Volume; the settings window behind it is not dimmed
With the fix: same dialog, the settings window behind it is dimmed (blocked)
Master: clicking Cancel on the settings window closes it, leaving the conflict dialog alone on screen
With the fix: after clicking the settings window's Cancel and its title-bar close button, both windows are still there
Master: whole sequence; Continue in the leftover dialog changes nothing
With the fix: whole sequence; Continue then OK saves Ctrl+F1 for Audio Volume
Master: tray settings reopened after Continue: Audio Volume still 'None'
With the fix: tray settings reopened after Continue and OK: Audio Volume shows Ctrl+F1

review.text: Real cause: the KMessageDialog had no transient parent, so Qt::WindowModal blocked nothing. Making it transient for the item's QQuickWindow is the usual way to parent a widget dialog to a QML window, and it's the same patch as the open MR kdeclarative!286. Before/after on the rig shows the window is now blocked and Continue stores the shortcut.
